claims.text: Machine-learning models using materials-science datasets can enable concurrent improvement of strength and ductility in metallic alloys.
Machine learning can optimize alloy composition to improve strength and ductility.
Machine learning can optimize processing conditions to improve strength and ductility.
The proposed method applies to as-cast or wrought metallic alloys exhibiting a strength–ductility trade-off.
The method is applicable over temperatures from -200 °C to 1000 °C.
The method is applicable over strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^2 s^-1.
Grain size is a structural mediator of the concurrent strength–ductility improvement.
Precipitate distribution is a structural mediator of the concurrent strength–ductility improvement.
Machine-learning models can identify compositions and processing conditions that refine grain size.
Machine-learning models can identify compositions and processing conditions that control precipitate distribution.
Grain refinement and control of precipitate distribution lead to improved strength and ductility.
The proposed method will increase strength by 20% relative to traditional alloy design and processing.
The proposed method will increase ductility by 30% relative to traditional alloy design and processing.
Machine-learning model accuracy depends on the quality of the training data.
Machine-learning model accuracy depends on the quantity of the training data.
Optimal compositions and processing conditions may vary between alloy systems.
